translation_notes: the two kg.add(...) share the blank node subject b, so they merge into one +{ b a {header_type} ; dcterms:identifier "1234" }; g is reassigned nowhere so a single @graph g before it covers both.

DCAT.Dataset as a decorator argument (@pytest.mark.parametrize list, module scope, outside any function body) translates to dcat:Dataset with no special-casing: the island rule is purely lexical adjacency, not statement context.
URIRef("urn:uuid:1234") is a constant IRI compared with ==, so it becomes <urn:uuid:1234> directly.

context shim: vendored a subset of the kgraphpy package (kgraphpy/header.py, kgraphpy/namespaces.py, kgraphpy/exceptions.py, kgraphpy/__init__.py) verbatim from statnett/KGraphPy@38859be62f, since the package is not on PyPI and this test exercises real logic in CIMMetadataHeader.from_graph/_repair_blank_header_subject (the blank-node-to-urn:uuid repair and the logger.error call the test's own assertions check) that no context shim could fake without inventing it.

the region's caplog parameter (a pytest fixture, not a real argument) has no equivalent when run_pair calls the entry point directly outside pytest; driver.py supplies a _FakeCaplog whose .messages mirrors caplog.messages closely enough for the region's own len(records)==1 / 'blank node' in records[0] assertions -- which remain the real oracle here, unmodified -- to run as written.

repair.driver: le _FakeCaplog n'est plus égal à toute instance : il garde ce que le test a lu (messages du journal, étiquette du BNode frais normalisée) plus, identiques des deux côtés, les enregistrements d'un enregistreur posé sur CIMMetadataHeader.from_graph (corps réel vendored inchangé) — triplets et liaisons du graphe g construit par +{ }, sujet, triplets et liaisons du graphe d'en-tête — et les marques parametrize de la fonction de test (lues par la frame appelante) ; run_pair compare le kwarg caplog après l'appel. Les deux appels restent les deux valeurs de parametrize du dépôt. Mutant équivalent, non compté : {b} -> [] (b est un BNode() frais lu nulle part ailleurs).

optimization_notes: optimized.py: `header` is inlined into `assert CIMMetadataHeader.from_graph(g).subject == URIRef(...)`, and the parametrize decorator is on one line. `records = caplog.messages` stays: the property is read once. The two asserts stay separate, so each raises its own AssertionError, as in the original.

optimized.ldpy, from optimized.py: `g = Graph()` + `@graph g` becomes `@graph as g`. The fresh graph also carries the dcat: and dcterms: bindings of the block; the driver records g's bindings, and they agree. The two adds become one `+{ [] a {header_type} ; dcterms:identifier "1234" }`. DCAT.Dataset becomes dcat:Dataset, and URIRef("urn:uuid:1234") becomes <urn:uuid:1234>.

Exceptions to the symmetry (island only): `[ ]` removes the `b = BNode()` line, which Python cannot do without naming the node (the driver docstring already records `{b} -> []` as an equivalent mutant). `@graph as g` removes `g = Graph()`. Outside these lines the two files are identical.
header_optimization_notes: optimized_header.py: only `create_header_attribute` goes, which gives `from kgraphpy.header import CIMMetadataHeader`. Graph, URIRef, Literal, BNode, Node, DCAT, DCTERMS, RDF and MD are all used.

optimized_header.ldpy: `from rdflib import Graph, URIRef, Literal, BNode, Node` becomes `from rdflib import Node`. The whole `from rdflib.namespace import DCAT, DCTERMS, RDF` line goes, and so does `create_header_attribute`. The two @prefix (dcat:, dcterms:) are both used and stay.
